scope: single standing resource; head revision only

inputs.role: existing sprite rendering/camera reference for initial generation only

initial.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE high-resolution transparent full-body standing battle-suit game resource for PROJECT V. Single still pose, not a motion sheet and not a poster.
Input 1 is the user's PRIMARY ARMOR DESIGN reference: preserve its recognizable cobalt/royal-blue, pearl-silver and black segmented powered armor, restrained antique-gold trim, narrow crowned helmet with tall swept blue fins, sharp wing-shaped shoulder plates, fitted articulated waist, long elegant white shin plates and tapered blue-black rear skirt panels. Preserve the tall, slender, adult HUMAN-WORN proportions, naturally sized head/hands/boots. This is a person in an advanced suit, not a giant robot, not chibi.
Input 2 is ONLY the SWORD DESIGN reference. Do NOT copy its black knight, fur, helmet, cape, armor or background. Create ONE imposing greatsword that closely follows this reference: very long, BROAD straight double-edged luminous ivory/white-metal blade, clearly pointed spear-like symmetrical tip, delicate continuous gold ornamental inlay down the blade center, sculpted gold sunburst crossguard with outward spikes, long dark wrapped grip and small faceted amber-gold pommel. Keep blade and grip a single rigid straight axis, no bends, no shortened or rounded tip, no blue sword substitution. Blade width and substantial length must clearly read as a greatsword.
Input 3 is ONLY the existing game's clean 2D cutout rendering, right-facing three-quarter camera and standing resource readability reference. Do NOT copy its armor, white fur, palette, cloak or sword.
Pose and framing: one complete character standing upright in a calm combat-ready idle stance, feet planted comfortably apart, slight three-quarter turn toward screen RIGHT, camera near torso height with a mild downward view rather than dramatic low-angle distortion. Right armored hand firmly wraps the sword grip near the hip, guard immediately in front of the fingers; the heavy greatsword points diagonally down toward the lower right, outside the torso silhouette, and the other hand rests naturally. Keep wrist and forearm connected and anatomically plausible. Chest armor, both legs and boots remain readable. Entire helmet spikes, rear panels, both soles and complete sword including sharp tip must fit inside the image with generous clean 6–8% transparent margins. Sword length about three quarters of standing figure height; provide enough canvas width, never shrink or chop the weapon to make it fit.
Rendering: polished high-end 2D semi-real game sprite illustration, crisp readable plate facets, controlled reflective metal, refined cobalt-blue enamel, black flexible joints, very restrained gold edging. Sharp professional cutout edges. The armor design and blue/silver balance must stay close to Input 1, with the distinctly ivory/gold greatsword from Input 2.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha across all empty areas and gaps, no backdrop, floor, podium, cast shadow, haze or checkerboard painted into the pixels. No aura cloud, floating debris, action trails or attack effects. Only restrained local emissive eyes and blade detail. No text, name, logos, watermark, labels, border or UI. One single complete character only. Prefer a large portrait canvas, approximately 1024 by 1536 or larger.

revision.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
This is a STRICT LOCAL HELMET CORRECTION of Image 1, a transparent full-body cobalt/silver battle-suit sprite. Output the same complete standing resource on the same 1024x1536 canvas.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. The user explicitly APPROVED EVERYTHING BELOW THE HEAD, including shoulders, neck/collar, chest, armor, arms, hands, fingers, sword grip, the entire greatsword shape and gold ornament, waist, skirt panels, legs, boots, colors, pose, viewpoint and all their placement. Preserve those pixels and proportions exactly. Do not repaint, restyle, sharpen, move or scale any of those approved elements. Keep the full image framing identical.
Image 2 is the ORIGINAL USER ARMOR REFERENCE. Use ONLY ITS HELMET/FACE DESIGN to correct Image 1. The current target helmet is inaccurate and must NOT remain the design reference.
Change only the helmet and the unwanted horns attached to the BACK of the head:
1. Completely REMOVE the enormous tall royal-blue spear/fin horns rising behind the helmet, particularly the very tall rear blade reaching near the top of the canvas and the extra rear blue/gold spikes. Do not replace them with other long horns, rear antennae or a taller crown. Restore empty transparent space where the removed head horns were. Keep the approved shoulder armor/fins intact; those are NOT head horns.
2. Closely match the compact, intricate silver-and-cobalt helmet in Image 2. Recreate its specific fine layered silver brow/crown around the small blue central forehead piece, narrow recessed eye/visor details, sculpted overlapping silver temple and cheek pieces, short refined silver lower face and jaw plates, and dark gaps separating those armor layers. Preserve subtle gold trim only where the ORIGINAL helmet has it. Avoid the current generic long smooth white beak/mask and large thick gold-edged facial band; those are the inaccurate details the user rejected. No exposed human face.
3. Keep the original reference's compact forward/side crest language at a modest scale, but NO added long horns behind the head. Match the original face armor's visual complexity and plate arrangement carefully rather than inventing a new helmet.
The corrected head must remain naturally connected to the exact existing neck at its current location, same head size and slightly right-facing three-quarter angle. Do not change the neck, shoulder plates or chest to fit it.
Maintain the existing transparent alpha and clean cutout edge. Keep all approved lower-body and greatsword pixels unchanged. No added background, aura, particles, text, labels, logo, second subject or cropped body. This is ONLY a head repair.

scaleRevision.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the provided current full-body transparent standing battle-suit resource with ONE tightly localized geometric change: enlarge the ENTIRE HEAD / HELMET by approximately 12.5% in BOTH width and height, a uniform scale factor of 1.125. This is a moderate proportional correction, not a new helmet or a chibi redesign.
The user likes the revised helmet design. Preserve that exact compact silver/cobalt forehead ornament, finely layered silver brow/cheek/jaw armor, eye details, small front/side crown fins and restrained gold trim. Keep the long rear horns REMOVED. Do not add any rear horns, extra crown spikes or new decorations.
ANCHOR the enlargement at the existing base-of-head/neck connection so the head grows slightly upward and sideways in place. Keep the head direction, three-quarter angle and expression exactly the same. Keep the neck/collar at the same position, adjusting only the tiny head-to-neck seam if necessary. Do not enlarge shoulders, collar, neck, chest or the whole character.
STRICTLY LOCK EVERYTHING ELSE in the reference: approved body, shoulder spikes, arms, hands, exact sword grip, entire straight ivory/gold greatsword and all its details, blue rear skirt panels, waist, legs, boots, all colors and textures, pose and framing. Do NOT regenerate or redesign these. Keep all non-head pixels in exactly the same canvas coordinates. Do NOT automatically recenter, zoom, rescale, shorten or move the figure when changing the head. The boots, sword tip and shoulder tips must retain their reference locations.
Keep the identical 1024x1536 canvas and transparent alpha. Full body and complete sword must remain visible. No new background, shadow, aura, effects, text, border or extra subjects. Output ONE full-body resource, not a comparison sheet. Only the head is about 12.5% bigger.
